- File: scripts/gh_helpers.sh
  Location: _autofix_pr_named_review_default_branch, second `resolved_default_branch="$(gh_retry gh api ...)"` capture (around lines 1197-1200)
  Issue: When `gh api --jq '.default_branch'` is applied to a response body that lacks the field, gh prints the literal string "null" rather than emitting nothing or exiting non-zero. The current whitespace/empty check (`[ -z ... ] || [[ ... =~ [[:space:][:cntrl:]] ]]`) accepts "null" as a valid branch name and the helper returns 0 with `pr_named_default_branch="null"`. No `AUTOFIX_PR_NAMED_REVIEW_PROVENANCE` log line is emitted; the PR-named filter then silently matches nothing and the peer/budget callers fall into their normal "no PR-named runs" path. While the GitHub `GET repos/<repo>` payload always carries `default_branch` on success and gh exits non-zero on 404, treating "null" as unresolved would close the corner case at one extra test clause.
  Suggested minimal fix: add a `[ "${resolved_default_branch}" = "null" ]` test to the rejection check so the helper returns 1 (and emits `AUTOFIX_PR_NAMED_REVIEW_PROVENANCE … outcome=default_branch_unresolved`) when gh's --jq output is the literal "null".
  Estimated lines changed: 2
  HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1
